first version: feedback for all 48 Privacy track submissions.

method: Scores are the judge-offset normalized averages from Stadium. "Strongest" and "weakest" compare each criterion with the track median for that criterion, so they show where a project stood out, not just its highest raw number.
Judges' notes are anonymised: no judge is named, and notes are paraphrased rather than quoted. Vague notes (for example a single word) are left out.

Every factual claim in a judge's note was checked before use. Claims that could be checked are listed under fact checks with their source. Claims that couldn't be checked are either dropped or worded as what a judge observed during judging.
Projects with no judge notes get feedback from their scores only, marked basis = scores.

projects.title: Zeno Wallet
projects.summary: Top prize, with high scores across the board. A judge praised its rare focus on a usability problem most privacy projects skip: a wallet that opens instantly and shows who can see what before you pay.
worked: A judge called the idea original and was impressed that it tackles a UX gap that usually gets overlooked.
Strong on every criterion. Works was near the maximum and Easy was well above the track median.
Nym routing is built into the code (Privacy Track Tech Review v1.0).
improve: One judge was concerned the fast-sync server could still learn something about users. Say exactly what the sync server sees today, and what it will stop seeing once attestation and the incoming-viewing-key mode in your milestone ship.

projects.title: Zec Start
projects.summary: Third prize. A judge saw it closing a real gap in basic onboarding: a first-timer reaches a real private payment in minutes.
worked: A judge found it easy, clear and concise. Easy was your strongest criterion, far above the track median.
A judge called onboarding one of the biggest gaps in the ecosystem.
improve: Teach more privacy-specific topics, for example what a viewing key reveals or why moving funds out of the shielded pool can link you.
A judge suggested ZecHub may want to integrate it. That conversation could give the lessons a permanent home.
Continuing sat at the track median. Your classroom plan is the strongest way to show the project keeps going.

facts.text: Your zingo-cli build turns Nym off, so the demo's network traffic isn't mixnet-routed. That may be worth a lesson of its own.
facts.source: Privacy Track Tech Review v1.0, Nym column

projects.title: Ghost Layer
projects.summary: Second prize. Judges saw a strong privacy improvement in an often-overlooked area: wallet syncing and sending can no longer be linked by the light-wallet server.
worked: Private was your strongest criterion and among the highest in the track.
Judges valued that it reduces linkability between syncing and sending transactions.
improve: Easy was your weakest criterion. A local gateway is a setup step most users won't take. Your milestone's "Ghost mode" inside an existing wallet is the most direct fix.

projects.title: Hisaab
projects.summary: Third prize. Judges agreed Zcash needs accounting tools and saw this as useful for real adoption.
worked: Works was your strongest criterion: the end-to-end flow from invoice to accountant-ready ledger ran.
improve: Get the first accountant to use it on real books. Your milestone says nobody has agreed yet, and that pilot is what proves the need.

projects.title: Mirage
projects.summary: Second prize. A judge found it more original than most, and best suited to living inside the wallets people already use.
worked: Private was your strongest criterion, well above the track median.
improve: Works was your weakest criterion, slightly below the median. Show the check working end to end on a real wallet flow.
A judge suggested it would work best inside popular wallets. Your planned pre-send pull request to zkool or Zingo is the right next step.

projects.title: zcash-now (MCP + llms.txt)
projects.summary: Ecosystem Prize. A judge liked the keyless, stdio-only design and saw it as a strong contribution to ZecHub and Zcash developers generally.
worked: Private and Continuing were both well above the track median.
improve: A judge noted it needs a maintainer. Say who keeps the recipes and facts current after the 30 days, since the daily checks need someone to review them.
Another team built a similar tool with the same name. Coordinating with them, or at least linking each other, would help developers.

projects.title: Whisper-Shop
projects.summary: A judge saw one of the better, working agentic-commerce flows: send shielded ZEC with a memo, get the code back.
worked: Works was at the maximum: judges confirmed the flow runs.
Another judge found it simple and effective.
improve: A judge asked what happens when the vendor doesn't deliver. Add a refund or dispute path, and say who holds funds in between.
Needed was your weakest criterion, below the median. Show who uses this over existing gift-card checkouts.

facts.text: Bitrefill doesn't accept ZEC directly. Paying from ZEC means swapping to USDC first, for example through NEAR Intents 1Click, which takes ZEC only from transparent addresses.
facts.source: Event Bitrefill developer docs (Ways to pay; Lane 5 route), checked 19 Oct 2026

projects.title: Shielded Shopping Agent

projects.title: Zool
projects.summary: A judge liked the idea of paying people in Zcash without collecting their wallet addresses, but wasn't sure how many users need it.

Continuing was your weakest criterion. Your milestone proposes a new GitHub-bounty feature rather than finishing the current one.
A judge suggested building on ZIP 324.

facts.text: ZIP 324, "URI-Encapsulated Payments", is a Draft ZIP for sending ZEC through a messaging app as a link that the recipient can claim without a wallet or address. That matches your use case.
facts.source: zips.z.cash/zip-0324 (status: Draft), checked 9 Nov 2026
